summary: Independent LLM review of the exact frozen statement and full proof, including the polytope facet-moment extension. The one-sided section moment inequality is proved by a valid equal-mass cone comparison: the root-density difference has at most one positive-to-negative crossing, and the support cannot exceed the comparison cone height. The d=1 case and affine coarea factors are correct. The resulting simplex barycentric centroid bound and its stretched-simplex sharpness example check exactly. Maximizing an inscribed simplex over compact vertex tuples gives an attained Q; applying the half-volume containment separately to every translated midpoint simplex proves the full reflection inclusion. The reflection is injective and volume preserving, so it pays the stated endpoint mass for every closed ambient halfspace, including pure integer normals. Distinct-fiber accounting and the scoped core comparison are valid. For polytopes, the facet coarea densities and first moments transform with the claimed reciprocal scaling and determinant factors; the eta criterion, eta<=1, cube/parallelotope sharpness construction, and threshold comparison in every dimension are correct. The cited classical cone-comparison source was independently checked; the argument is self-contained rather than dependent on that citation.
target_match_explanation: This is a scoped ordinary-geometric containment theorem with explicit mixed reflection and parity-core consequences. It does not assert the simplex-volume or facet-moment partner hypothesis for arbitrary mixed-integer sets, and it does not treat intrinsic lower-dimensional fibers or d=0. It is therefore an auxiliary result rather than a resolution of the locked general target. Review method: independent LLM mathematical verification.
